subject: Chemistry
description: Solute, solvent, concentration, molarity, types of solutions

questions.stem: In a solution of SUGAR in WATER, sugar is the:
questions.explanation: SOLUTION = SOLUTE + SOLVENT. SOLUTE — substance DISSOLVED (less amount, smaller component). SOLVENT — substance that DOES the dissolving (more amount, the medium). EXAMPLES: SUGAR (solute) in water (solvent); SALT (solute) in water (solvent); ALCOHOL (solute or solvent depending on which is more); GASES dissolved in water (CO₂ in cola, O₂ in seawater for fish). UNIVERSAL SOLVENT = water (dissolves more substances than any other solvent — due to its polarity + hydrogen bonding ability). TYPES OF SOLUTIONS: solid in liquid (sugar-water); liquid in liquid (alcohol-water); gas in liquid (CO₂-water); solid in solid (alloys: brass = Cu+Zn); etc.

options.option_text: Moles of solute per LITRE of solution
Moles of solute per kg of solvent (molality)
Mass of solute per litre of solution
Volume of solute per litre of solvent

questions.explanation: MOLARITY (M) = moles of solute / VOLUME of solution (in litres). UNIT: mol/L or M. Most common concentration measure. KEY: based on volume of WHOLE SOLUTION (not just solvent). Temperature-DEPENDENT (volume changes with T). MOLALITY (m) = moles of solute / mass of solvent (in kg) — temperature-INDEPENDENT (mass doesn't change with T). NORMALITY (N) = gram-equivalents of solute per litre of solution (used in acid-base, redox titrations). MOLE FRACTION (x) = moles of one component / total moles. PPM = parts per million (10⁻⁶ — used for trace amounts; e.g., water hardness, air pollution). PPB = parts per billion (10⁻⁹ — even more dilute). %w/w, %v/v, %w/v — common percent forms.

questions.stem: A SATURATED solution is one where:

options.option_text: No more solute can dissolve at given temp
Lots more solute can still dissolve

questions.explanation: SATURATED — solution containing maximum solute that can dissolve at given TEMPERATURE; any more added → undissolved. UNSATURATED — less than max → can dissolve more. SUPERSATURATED — temporarily holding MORE than max (unstable; tiny disturbance → crystallises out). SOLUBILITY = max solute that can dissolve in given solvent at given T. TEMPERATURE EFFECT: most solids' solubility INCREASES with T (sugar dissolves more in hot tea); GAS solubility DECREASES with T (warm cola loses fizz; that's why tropical seas have less dissolved O₂, fewer fish per area than cold waters — counter-intuitive but true). PRESSURE EFFECT: gases — Henry's law (solubility ∝ pressure; that's why opening soda bottle releases CO₂).

questions.explanation: BRINE = concentrated salt water (NaCl solution; typically 3.5%+ — sea water is brine). USES: PRESERVATION (pickling fish, vegetables — high salt prevents bacteria growth, due to osmotic stress on microbes), brining meats (Thanksgiving turkey), DE-ICING roads (salt lowers freezing point of water). INDUSTRIAL: source of sodium + chlorine (electrolysis = chlor-alkali process → NaOH + Cl₂ + H₂). Salt also kept on Indian wedding plates as 'shagun' for some ceremonies; in Goa, salt pans (sea-water evaporation) yield commercial salt. SEA WATER: ~3.5% salt; DEAD SEA: 33%+; SAMBHAR LAKE: ~22%. INSIGHT — salt's role in HISTORY: Roman soldiers' 'salarium' (= salary, paid in salt); Gandhi's 1930 Salt March (Dandi) protested British salt tax.

questions.stem: TYNDALL EFFECT (scattering of light in colloidal solution) is shown by:
questions.explanation: TYNDALL EFFECT — light beam SCATTERS visibly when passing through COLLOIDAL solution (1-1000 nm particle size); not in TRUE solutions. EXAMPLES of colloids showing it: MILK (fat droplets in water — emulsion), FOG (water droplets in air), SMOKE (carbon particles in air), JELLY, BUTTER, BLOOD, MIST, AEROSOL, FOAM. WHY: particles BIG ENOUGH to scatter visible light (~400-700 nm), but small enough to stay suspended (don't settle). VISIBLE RAY OF SUNLIGHT through DUSTY ROOM (light beam visible) = same effect. NIGHT SKY appears blue from atmospheric scattering (Rayleigh scattering for molecules < 1 nm; Tyndall for larger particles 1-1000 nm). True solutions (salt, sugar) — particles ~0.1 nm — too small to scatter; light passes through unaffected.

questions.stem: Solubility of a GAS in liquid INCREASES with:

options.option_text: Pure water without solutes only (option here)

questions.explanation: GAS SOLUBILITY in liquid: (1) DIRECTLY proportional to PRESSURE (HENRY's LAW: P = k·x, where x = mole fraction). Open soda bottle → pressure drops → CO₂ comes out (fizz!). (2) INVERSELY proportional to TEMPERATURE (warm coke = flat). EXAMPLES: SCUBA divers must surface SLOWLY — 'BENDS' (decompression sickness): N₂ dissolved in blood at high pressure (deep) comes out as bubbles when returning to surface (lower pressure). Treated in HYPERBARIC chamber. WHY ICE WATER for fish tank? COOL water holds MORE dissolved O₂. ALSO: BOILED water = removes dissolved gases (taste 'flat'); explains why high-altitude tea + coffee taste different (lower pressure).

questions.explanation: DISTILLATION — separates LIQUIDS based on different BOILING POINTS. Heat mixture; lower-bp liquid evaporates first, condense vapour back (cool tube), collect. SIMPLE distillation: liquids with bp difference > 25°C. FRACTIONAL distillation: closer bps (used in petroleum refining — separates crude oil into petrol/kerosene/diesel/lubricants). DISTILLED WATER — pure water, gases removed, used in batteries, lab. DESALINATION (Saudi Arabia, Israel, UAE) — distill seawater for fresh water. ALCOHOL distillation — Indian liquor industry. PYQ FAVOURITE — separation methods: FILTRATION (insoluble solid from liquid), CHROMATOGRAPHY (mixture of dyes/inks), CRYSTALLISATION (purify solids), MAGNETIC SEPARATION (iron from sand), CENTRIFUGATION (cream from milk), SUBLIMATION (camphor from sand).
